doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Practicing in the shower room and Arthur Merriweather at the Club Baron
summary: Caught playing Goodman solos at A&T, he practiced in the shower room and later joked with trumpeter Arthur Merriweather at the Club Baron.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yes, I do. I was at the Club Baron one night, and this guy, Arthur Merriweather... I played with him at North Carolina A&T, in the band. He was a great trumpet player. We had a jazz orchestra and everything. What happened, they caught me playing in the band room some Benny Goodman solos, and they took away my privileges. So I didn’t have anywhere to practice. So in the middle of the day, when everybody else was at class, I’d go into the shower room and practice. He used to come by and say, “Oh, you’re the shithouse clarinet player.” I used to tell him, “All right, one of these days you’re going to have...” When I was at the Club Barron, the guy said, “A guy is at the door from A&T that knows you who says he wants to get in.” So I went out and I saw him. I said, “I don’t know him.” Ha- ha. “Don’t let him in; I don’t know him.” After I finished playing a couple of tunes, I saw him sitting in there. He’d gone out to the car and got a picture of the band from A&T, and brought it back to the door and showed the guy. [LAUGHS]
I was sitting right by him in the band. [LAUGHS] I cracked up.
Did you acknowledge his existence at that point?
Oh yeah. Of course. Of course. He was a great guy.
